ctx.x: Well, Bunk Johnson was supposed to be an old-time man who taught... Well, Joe Oliver. Joe Oliver in turn taught... Larry Armstrong. And that's how it goes. Nobody else played music but the syndicates, the Negroes. Nobody played music in New Orleans. As far as I know about music, and if you want the truth about it, the Negroes did not play any kind of music equal to white men at any time. Even the poorest band of white men played better than the Negroes in my days. With the exception of like Piron and...

Robichaud and there wasn't another one. Manuel Perez had a note-reading band. And they played by notes. They played almost the same as white men. They had nothing to it. They played just what was on the paper, like on a score. They say different today. That's not so. Never has been so. And Negroes never has been in the sentence in the music field until only lately. Some time ago they had an article in the item. What they didn't say about poor Evelyn Presley, I couldn't begin to tell you.
